greeting.text: Hello, hello! I am {npc}, goddess of the hearth and head of the whole Hestia Familia, which at the moment is me, one stubborn boy and a great deal of enthusiasm. Who are you, {player}?
A visitor! Do sit... well, there is only one chair, and it is mine. I am {npc}. What can a goddess do for you?
Back again, {player}! Have you been feeding yourself properly? Nobody ever does.
Oh, it is you. I was telling Bell about you. Nothing bad, I promise. Mostly.
Careful in the Dungeon, {player}. I cannot bless everyone, but I can worry about everyone.

hint.text: A god may not use power in the lower world. We can advise, scold and bake. I do two of those well.
Strength grows faster against something just above you than against something far below. It also kills you faster, so choose with care.
The Dungeon is alive in its way, and it learns. When you grow, it grows. Do not let that make you proud; let it make you curious.
Bell collects trouble the way other people collect coins. Tell him to rest, please. He never listens to me.
If anything with horns turns up on the upper floors, you have my permission to run. Goddesses are allowed to say such things.
Welf has been muttering about a black giant. When a smith mutters, a hammer is never far behind.
The Water City, two heads. I do not like it. Two heads means two opinions, and both of them are wrong.
Udaeus. Bones. I really dislike bones. Please do not bring any home.
That is the lot, then. I am very proud. Insufferably so. Come and be insufferable with me.

farewell.text: Come back soon, {player}, and bring snacks.
Do not do anything I would not do. Or anything I would, really.
Goodbye! Wave at the Dungeon for me.
